key_insight: The paper computes steady lid-driven cavity flows with a linearized iterative FEM solver and assesses their stability by checking whether perturbation eigenvalues acquire positive real parts.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to verify when high-Reynolds-number cavity-flow steady states are numerically reliable or become unstable, which matters for CFD validation and solver design.
method: Linearize the nonlinear convective term and solve a sequence of linear boundary-value problems until convergence.
Discretize the steady flow and perturbation equations with finite elements on triangular meshes.
Form a generalized algebraic eigenvalue problem for perturbations; positive-real-part eigenvalues signal instability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports calculations on a sequence of refined meshes over various Reynolds numbers for square-cavity flow, using the eigenvalue spectrum to judge stability.
watch_item: Stability conclusions may depend on mesh refinement and the accuracy of the linearization/eigenvalue solve, especially at high Reynolds numbers.
paper_title: Stability analysis of the steady solution for incompressible lid-driven cavity flow
